body: “I t means more than just three points. It’s for the whole club. It’s for the whole place. It’s for the whole of Tottenham.” One only needs to be in the presence of Tottenham Hotspur’s Cathinka Tandberg for a few minutes to feel the passion that emanates from her when it comes to this weekend’s north London derby. As a lifelong Spurs fan, the forward understands more than most the intensity of the rivalry that exists between her side and Arsenal, one that she cannot wait to experience once again on Saturday.
“It will just be an incredible feeling,” she tells Moving the Goalposts. “I think you will feel a few nerves that you maybe don’t feel in a normal game but that’s good.”

“All the Spurs fans hate Arsenal and Arsenal hate Spurs. That’s how it is. You want to show that you’re the best team. Simple as that. You just want to fight for the club, the badge and for the people around you.”

body: Howe left Newcastle in late July to take a break from the game but would seriously consider a return for the United role, it is understood, should this be offered.
Howe would be less expensive to bring in than Unai Emery, another admired candidate, because Aston Villa would demand about £20m in compensation for their manager.

In five years managing Newcastle Howe impressed, leading the team to the 2025 Carabao Cup, ending a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. After taking over from Steve Bruce in November 2021, Howe led Newcastle to 11th, winning 12 of the last 18 games. The team had gone 14 games without a victory at the start of the season.
Howe also took Newcastle back into the Champions League after 20 years in 2023 and qualified again two seasons later. He managed Bournemouth for five seasons in the Premier League from 2015.

articles.title: Should Man Utd boss Carrick drop captain Fernandes?
articles.summary: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick must decide whether to leave skipper Bruno Fernandes out of Sunday's crucial Premier League clash with Bournemouth
body: Michael Carrick is never short of advice around how he should do his job as head coach of Manchester United.
Few of his players divide opinion quite so much as skipper Bruno Fernandes.
So, it stands to reason there are a variety of views around whether Fernandes should be dropped for Sunday's vital Premier League game against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

"It is a big problem for Michael," he told The Overlap podcast. "Put people in the team you trust. Your captain has thrown you under the bus. If you don't think he is playing for you, get him out. I wouldn't pick him even though he is their best player."

articles.title: Asian Football Confederation backs Gianni Infantino in U-turn on Fifa presidency
articles.summary: AFC president Sheikh Salman praises and hugs Infantino. It had stood with Uefa and Concacaf against him. The Asian Football Confederation has endorsed Gianni Infantino for another term as Fifa’s president in a turnaround in its stance from two months ago when it criticised the head of football’s…
body: The AFC president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, speaking at the body’s extraordinary congress in Tokyo on Friday, embraced Infantino with a large hug in front of the membership as he delivered his endorsement.

“We affirm our full commitment to supporting you and your leadership as you seek a new mandate as the Fifa president.” Sheikh Salman said. “You’ve visited a lot of countries in Asia. I’ve spoken to a lot of members within this continent. I know your feeling and I think your commitment is clear as well.”

The AFC has 47 member associations. Even if all the members do not follow the direction of Sheikh Salman, those votes could be a key to guaranteeing another mandate for Infantino. The Fifa election is in March and nominations close on 18 November. So far no one is standing against him.

Addressing his remarks to Infantino, Sheikh Salman indicated not every AFC member would go along with the endorsement but that most will. “My feeling is, I’m sure, the feeling of most of my members,” he said. “And I’ve said that to you.”

articles.summary: Nottingham Forest go to Ipswich in the bottom three of the Premier League, but boss Oliver Glasner believes they have deserved more this season.
body: "It feels unfair but I don't want to be complaining and feeling as victims."
Oliver Glasner's words offer a positive outlook as he believes Nottingham Forest deserve more following their disappointing start to the season.
They visit Ipswich Town on Friday following three straight defeats during an underwhelming opening which has left them in the Premier League's relegation zone.

articles.summary: Those following Chelsea closely may feel history is repeating itself as Pedro Neto excels at wing-back, much like Victor Moses did a decade ago.
body: Just as they did 10 years ago, Chelsea are thriving after moving a winger into a wing-back role, with Pedro Neto the latest player to benefit.
A decade ago, it was Victor Moses who made the switch, adapting to Antonio Conte's then-innovative system and helping Chelsea to a 13-match winning run en route to the Premier League title in 2017.
Neto scored twice from wing-back in Chelsea 's 2-0 win at Everton 's Hill Dickinson Stadium on Saturday.
Chelsea did not regard the Portuguese as untouchable during the summer, although they had set a lofty asking price of about £100m.

articles.title: Remembering Kaziu Deyna: City's Polish pioneer
articles.summary: On this day in 1947, a Manchester City pioneer and one of post-war Europe’s most gifted attacking midfield talents was born.Kaziu Deyna was a the Polish footballing legend.Though injury meant that h...
body: Though injury meant that he only played 43 times for the Club during his short stay in Manchester, Deyna was one of the early trailblazers for the thousands of overseas players who have subsequently brought so much to our domestic game.
It’s easy to forget now but the arrival at Maine Road of the quiet, unassuming man from Starogard Gdanski made international headlines back in 1978.
Kaziu arrived at the Club following that year’s World Cup finals in Argentina armed with a reputation for being one of the European football’s most accomplished dynamic midfielders.
A gold medallist at the 1972 Olympic Games and a silver medal winner at the 1976 Games, Deyna had also finished third in the 1974 Ballon d’Or award, behind Johan Cruyff and Franz Beckenbauer.

articles.title: Kenny Atkinson admits Cavaliers were ‘depressed’ after LeBron James chose 76ers
articles.summary: Kenny Atkinson has admitted the Cleveland Cavaliers were left “depressed” after LeBron James chose the Philadelphia 76ers over a potential reunion with his former team.
body: The Cavaliers coach revealed that Cleveland had been anticipating James’ arrival and was excited about the possibility of working with the NBA superstar again.
Instead, James joined Philadelphia, leaving Atkinson to come to terms with missing out on a player he had hoped to bring into his plans.
Speaking to ESPN’s Dave McMenamin, Atkinson described the disappointment of expecting a free-agent move to happen before learning that it would not.

He said: “We were anticipating and excited to land LeBron and then you have that news, having gone through free agency a lot, when you’re expecting something to happen and it doesn’t happen, that first day or two, you’re just like, you’re depressed, quite honestly.”

articles.title: 'Out of control' - Verstappen criticises 'unacceptable' track surface
articles.summary: Max Verstappen revealed concerns over the state of his spine as he unleashed a scathing criticism of the "out of control" bumpy track surface at Circuit of The Americas.
body: The four-time world champion arrives in Austin for Sunday's United States Grand Prix after claiming his first two victories of the season in back-to-back races.
Speaking to the media on Thursday, Verstappen was unexpectedly passionate over the state of the circuit, which is generally considered as one of the most popular among the drivers on the F1 calendar.
"You can also see the track conditions. From what I saw in the WEC [World Endurance Championship], the circuit was extremely bumpy," Verstappen said.

"I'm not really looking forward to that to be honest, for your spine. I was joking about that in the last race but it's not really a joke to be honest because we mentioned this already for years that it's actually getting a bit out of control.

articles.title: Norris: 'Incredible' Antonelli two levels above Russell all season
articles.summary: Lando Norris believes Kimi Antonelli has done an "incredible job" and performed "two levels above" Mercedes team-mate George Russell this season, in form which has taken the Italian to the brink of a record-breaking world championship triumph.
body: Antonelli looks all but assured to succeed Norris as F1's reigning world champion this year thanks to the 102-point lead he holds at the top of the standings with six races left.

The 20-year-old could become the sport's youngest-ever champion as early as this Sunday's United States Grand Prix if he wins the race and nearest challengers Russell and Lewis Hamilton do not score sufficient points to stay in mathematical contention.
And Norris, who claimed his own maiden crown with McLaren last year, has spoken glowingly about Antonelli's second season of F1 up against the "very good" Russell.
"I think it's very impressive what he's been able to do," said Norris.

articles.title: Reporter Notebook: No panic stations at Sunderland despite tough start
articles.summary: It's certainly been a different start to the season for Sunderland compared to last year, when they flew out of the traps on their Premier League return and went months without a home league defeat.
body: This time around they sit bottom of the pile with four points from seven games. Things were always going to be tough with the additional load of European football to contend with, something Sunderland haven't experienced in over 50 years.
The performance at Bournemouth on Sunday, fresh from an away Europa league clash in Portugal, was littered with mistakes and individual errors.

It led to defender Nordi Mukiele suggesting post-match that the team had become "arrogant". That felt like the wrong choice of words from the Frenchman. I don't detect that mindset, but without doubt the schedule, both mentally and physically, is having an effect.
There was a feeling from within the club that those exertions of European football would be challenging this season, and that is playing out in the results.
